bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Open income-tax search and pending assessments — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to Note 50, describing search operations carried out by the Income Tax Department at various business premises of the Company in November 2023. The Company subsequently received notices and orders for various assessment years and has furnished details, filed appeals or rectification applications; for certain assessment years the Department is yet to complete the assessments. Management has assessed that the search and the assessment/reassessment are not likely to have any material adverse impact on the financial position, and the auditor's conclusion is not modified - but the matter remains unresolved.
- Product quality and material-science innovation risk in cookware — Global consumer trends are shifting towards non-toxic and 'clean' cookware, and the BRSR material-issues table states that failing to innovate in material science poses a market-share risk. Mitigation is a dual strategy of material innovation - a transition to Teflon-free ceramic coatings and the introduction of Cera-Steel hybrids - and field intelligence through the Product Service Group, which provides real-time market feedback.
- Dependence on the labour and social-compliance standards demanded by global retail partners — The BRSR flags Human Rights & Fair Labor Practices as both risk and opportunity: any violation of labour standards such as unsafe working conditions or lack of social security presents severe legal and reputational risk, while holistic welfare satisfies the ethical audit requirements of global partners like IKEA and Walmart. Mitigation is strict adherence to the IKEA IWAY framework, with dormitory housing for 350+ workers, free meals at the on-site canteen and contract buses for rural connectivity. 'Qualified Supplier' status - and with it long-term global export contracts - depends on maintaining these standards.
- Occupational health and safety at manufacturing operations — The BRSR identifies Health & Safety as a risk: neglecting it could lead to workplace accidents, legal penalties and reputational damage, resulting in financial losses and operational disruptions. Mitigation runs through health and safety policies, regular audits, strict compliance with standards, multi-stage inspections and random sampling (with non-conforming items scrapped), plus induction and monthly safety training.
- Data security and protection of intellectual property — The Company holds important intellectual property including product designs, processes and trade secrets; the BRSR flags that insufficient data security measures expose it to cyberattacks, hacking or internal threats leading to theft or unauthorised access. Controls cited are access control, virus protection, intrusion detection, data backups, authentication, monitoring, periodic reviews and data classification guidelines.
- Execution risk on the IKEA export platform, whose revenue and returns are still ahead — The IKEA partnership requires cookware developed to stringent quality, compliance and testing requirements, including the transition from conventional PTFE non-stick coatings to ceramic alternatives. Rs 58 crore has already been invested in dedicated tooling, machinery and supporting infrastructure, but production and revenue recognition are only expected to commence progressively from FY 2026-27 following the completion of stringent testing and approval processes - so the spend is sunk ahead of the earnings, and the stated expectations of improved capacity utilisation and EBITDA contribution comparable to or better than the domestic business remain unproven.
- Macroeconomic, trade-policy and geopolitical exposure — The MD&A notes that the pace of global expansion remains uncertain amid geopolitical tensions, trade policy uncertainty and uneven regional performance, and that economic policy uncertainty - particularly around global trade policies and tariffs - is expected to remain elevated through 2026, potentially affecting investment and trade flows. World trade volume growth is expected to decline from 4.1% in 2025 to 2.6% in 2026. This matters for a company building an export platform.
- Reliance on an internal risk-management framework rather than disclosed risk quantification — The Board's Report states that the business is exposed to internal and external risks identified and revisited every year, managed through a Risk Management Policy, a well-defined risk framework and a Risk Management Committee, with SOPs and a Risk Control Matrix designed for critical processes and internal financial controls tested through management's ongoing monitoring. A Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy is in place. The disclosure describes structure but names no quantified exposure, so the risk register itself is not visible to an outside reader.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Stove Kraft operates two ISO 9001:2015 certified manufacturing facilities - a larger one in Bengaluru, Karnataka and another in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh. The Bengaluru plant spans roughly 53 acres, with about one acre kept aside for future expansion, and houses supplementary backward-integration units producing glass lids, weight valves, vent tubes and gaskets; adjacent to the factory and registered office the Company operates a 1.20 lakh sq ft warehouse on 2.75 acres with storage capacity of around 25,500 pallet positions. Baddi manufactures Inner Lid Cookers. Management describes the investment of the last five years in backward-integrated manufacturing as being aimed at overcoming supply disruptions and improving gross margins, and states that the major investment cycle is now substantially complete - the capacity created provides headroom for a considerably larger business without requiring a proportionate increase in capital expenditure, making improving utilisation the driver of operating leverage, returns and cash generation over coming years. Against the IKEA supply partnership for cookware for IKEA's global store network, the Company has built a dedicated 1,80,000 sq ft manufacturing facility at Harohalli, Karnataka and invested approximately Rs 58 crore in dedicated tooling, machinery and supporting infrastructure; three product lines have been awarded, the business is expected to commence shortly, and production and revenue recognition are expected to commence progressively during FY 2026-27, with meaningful revenue contribution seen in the coming years. A Cast Iron Foundry at the Harohalli factory runs an automated line with current installed capacity of 2.2 million pieces per annum, designed to reach 4.4 million pieces per annum in future. The Company began manufacturing and selling kitchen chimneys from its own plant in Q1 FY26 and is building a full in-house manufacturing setup for all kinds of chimney, expected to take around a year, in a category placed under a Quality Control Order making BIS mandatory from 2026. Manufacturing capability is also being strengthened across Bengaluru and Baddi to support induction-cooktop demand, and production of backward-integrated kettles and cast-iron cookware was increased during FY 2025-26. On the retail side, 67 new stores were opened in FY 2025-26 taking the network to 329 outlets across 151 cities and 22 states (147 of them franchisee-operated), with a plan to add around 100 stores nationwide every year, increasingly through franchisee-operated formats focused on North and West India. On energy infrastructure, the upcoming commissioning of a 1.7 MW solar plant is expected shortly, and the Company has commissioned an RO plant and a 500 KL STP as part of a closed-loop water system.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing movement towards electric cooking - induction cooktops, rice cookers, air fryers and other electric appliances becoming more relevant as households seek speed, convenience and energy efficiency; induction cooktops delivered 23.9% value growth and 11.7% volume growth in FY 2025-26, with growth accelerating further in the fourth quarter
- Formalisation of India's consumer durables market, expected to grow at approximately 11% CAGR through FY 2028-29, aided by Make in India, production-linked incentives, GST rationalisation, energy labelling, BIS certification and tighter safety standards
- Modular kitchen adoption making hobs, chimneys and built-in solutions more relevant; premiumisation as branded cookware becomes a lifestyle statement
- Tier II and Tier III cities emerging as important consumption centres as brand awareness, aspirations and access to modern products increase
- E-commerce, quick commerce, digital payments, modern retail and exclusive stores becoming interconnected parts of the consumer journey, with digitally active consumers discovering products through social content and marketplaces
- Rising disposable incomes, especially in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities, with non-food expenditure now accounting for 60% of urban consumption
- Health and wellness trends supporting demand for air fryers, steamers and alternative cooking formats, and for non-stick and specialised cookware
- Own retail contributing 7.5% of revenue, with exclusive brand outlets improving product visibility and providing direct consumer insight
- Working-capital discipline: cycle reduced from 64 days to 23 days and net debt reduced, giving greater financial flexibility for the next phase of capacity utilisation, category expansion and market development
- Headwinds acknowledged: uneven consumer demand across quarters, international trade uncertainty, commodity-price movements and foreign exchange volatility affecting the operating environment
- Indian macro backdrop cited as supportive - real GDP of 7.6% in FY 2025-26, benign inflation and an unchanged repo rate of 5.50%
- Chimney and other built-in categories supported by BIS certification and tighter safety standards raising the barrier for unorganised players
- Under the IKEA partnership the Company has been awarded three product lines, with production and revenue recognition expected to commence progressively during FY 2026-27; no order-book value is disclosed.

currentContext.expansion: Stove Kraft operates two ISO 9001:2015 certified manufacturing facilities - a larger one in Bengaluru, Karnataka and another in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh. The Bengaluru plant spans roughly 53 acres, with about one acre kept aside for future expansion, and houses supplementary backward-integration units producing glass lids, weight valves, vent tubes and gaskets; adjacent to the factory and registered office the Company operates a 1.20 lakh sq ft warehouse on 2.75 acres with storage capacity of around 25,500 pallet positions. Baddi manufactures Inner Lid Cookers. Management describes the investment of the last five years in backward-integrated manufacturing as being aimed at overcoming supply disruptions and improving gross margins, and states that the major investment cycle is now substantially complete - the capacity created provides headroom for a considerably larger business without requiring a proportionate increase in capital expenditure, making improving utilisation the driver of operating leverage, returns and cash generation over coming years. Against the IKEA supply partnership for cookware for IKEA's global store network, the Company has built a dedicated 1,80,000 sq ft manufacturing facility at Harohalli, Karnataka and invested approximately Rs 58 crore in dedicated tooling, machinery and supporting infrastructure; three product lines have been awarded, the business is expected to commence shortly, and production and revenue recognition are expected to commence progressively during FY 2026-27, with meaningful revenue contribution seen in the coming years. A Cast Iron Foundry at the Harohalli factory runs an automated line with current installed capacity of 2.2 million pieces per annum, designed to reach 4.4 million pieces per annum in future. The Company began manufacturing and selling kitchen chimneys from its own plant in Q1 FY26 and is building a full in-house manufacturing setup for all kinds of chimney, expected to take around a year, in a category placed under a Quality Control Order making BIS mandatory from 2026. Manufacturing capability is also being strengthened across Bengaluru and Baddi to support induction-cooktop demand, and production of backward-integrated kettles and cast-iron cookware was increased during FY 2025-26. On the retail side, 67 new stores were opened in FY 2025-26 taking the network to 329 outlets across 151 cities and 22 states (147 of them franchisee-operated), with a plan to add around 100 stores nationwide every year, increasingly through franchisee-operated formats focused on North and West India. On energy infrastructure, the upcoming commissioning of a 1.7 MW solar plant is expected shortly, and the Company has commissioned an RO plant and a 500 KL STP as part of a closed-loop water system.

one-line thesis: Stove Kraft leveraged geopolitical tailwinds (Iran war, US tariff cuts) and backward integration to drive 32.4% Q4 revenue growth, with induction cooktops surging 89.4% YoY. The commencement of IKEA billing and a shift to franchise-led retail expansion position the company for sustained >15% CAGR, though near-term PAT is suppressed by forex volatility and accounting changes on lease liabilities.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 414.5 Cr (+32.4% YoY); EBITDA: INR 39.5 Cr (+33.9% YoY), Margin 9.5% (+113 bps YoY); PAT: INR 6.1 Cr (+317.8% YoY, base effect) but margin only 1.5% due to ~INR 10-12 Cr one-off forex loss and increased interest from sale-leaseback; Order Book: Implicitly strong with induction demand exceeding 4-5 Mn unit capacity; Net Debt: Reduced via repayment, but interest charges rose to INR 25 Cr due to lease liability accounting and suppliers' credit interest.
guidance: Revenue Growth: >15% for FY27 (confidence in 30% run-rate); Margin: Protect 11% EBITDA, target 42% Gross Margin in 2-3 years (+1% annually); Order Inflow: Induction demand > capacity; Capex: ~INR 40 Cr for FY27 (maintenance & minor lines), major cycle complete.
order book & pipeline: Demand for induction cooktops exceeds current 4-5 Mn unit annualized capacity; IKEA pipeline valued at INR 200-250 Cr at full capacity (3 lines phasing in through FY27); Export orders normalizing post-tariff reduction.
segment / subsidiary detail: Induction Cooktops: 15.5% of revenue, +89.4% value growth, +67.3% volume growth; Small Appliances: 40.2% of revenue, +12.7% value growth, +97.7% volume growth (mix shift to lower ASP items); Cookware: Strong premiumization from aluminum to stainless steel; HoReCa: New 3,500W infrared launch.
growth verticals / optionality: IKEA global sourcing (INR 200-250 Cr potential); US export market reopening (tariff drop to 18%); Retail store network scaling to 500 by 2027 (currently 329); Capacity utilization upside beyond 5 Mn units.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin stable at 38.6% despite commodity inflation (Aluminum/Steel) due to 10% price hikes passed in Q4; EBITDA margin expanded 113 bps to 9.5%; Opex grew 41% YoY driven by sales commissions (franchise model), freight, and warranty provisions aligned with 32% sales growth.
capex / expansion: FY26 capitalized capex INR 111 Cr (net cash outflow ~INR 70-75 Cr after supplier credit); Major cycle complete; FY27 guidance ~INR 40 Cr for retail expansion and minor assembly line tweaks; IKEA plant fully capitalized as of Mar '26.
capital allocation: Debt repayment prioritized; Shift to Franchise-Owned/Franchise-Operated (FOFO) and Company-Owned/Franchise-Operated (COFO) models to reduce capital intensity of retail expansion; Inventory stocking (45-60 days) for raw materials to hedge against metal price inflation.
risks & watch-items: Forex volatility (significant loss in Q4); Raw material price inflation (Aluminum, Steel, Glass); Supply chain dependency on Chinese components (crystalline glass, magnets); Competition in e-commerce channel; Execution risk on rapid retail franchise rollout.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on volume growth (>15% guidance); Pragmatic on margins (protecting 11% EBITDA while absorbing forex hits); Transparent on accounting distortions (lease liability, supplier credit); Focused on market share leadership in induction.
non-obvious takeaways: Retail store average sales increased from INR 3.8L to INR 4.7L, with breakeven at INR 2.5L, making new stores immediately accretive; Right-of-Use assets dropped from INR 160 Cr to INR 62 Cr due to accounting change (useful life reduced from 9 to 3 years), artificially depressing assets/liabilities; 97.7% volume growth in small appliances vs 12.7% value growth indicates a strategic mix shift to high-volume, lower-ASP entry-level products to capture market share.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Stove Kraft is a Bengaluru-headquartered kitchen and home solutions company with over two decades of industry experience, selling under the Pigeon, Gilma and BLACK+DECKER brands across 28 states and 6 Union Territories and exporting to 14 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells kitchen and home solutions under three primary brands - Pigeon, Gilma and BLACK+DECKER - addressing the value, semi-premium and premium segments respectively. It holds a notable presence in pressure cookers and a leading market share in free-standing hobs, cooktops and non-stick cookware, and has extended into cast-iron, tri-ply, ceramic-coated and stainless-steel cookware, small appliances and in-house manufactured kitchen chimneys. Products reach individual households through general trade, modern retail, e-commerce, quick commerce and exclusive brand outlets, while the Company also acts as an OEM for global retailers and supplies institutional, defence and paramilitary canteen customers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Growing movement towards electric cooking - induction cooktops, rice cookers, air fryers and other electric appliances becoming more relevant as households seek speed, convenience and energy efficiency; induction cooktops delivered 23.9% value growth and 11.7% volume growth in FY 2025-26, with growth accelerating further in the fourth quarter
- Formalisation of India's consumer durables market, expected to grow at approximately 11% CAGR through FY 2028-29, aided by Make in India, production-linked incentives, GST rationalisation, energy labelling, BIS certification and tighter safety standards
- Modular kitchen adoption making hobs, chimneys and built-in solutions more relevant; premiumisation as branded cookware becomes a lifestyle statement
- Tier II and Tier III cities emerging as important consumption centres as brand awareness, aspirations and access to modern products increase
- E-commerce, quick commerce, digital payments, modern retail and exclusive stores becoming interconnected parts of the consumer journey, with digitally active consumers discovering products through social content and marketplaces
- Rising disposable incomes, especially in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities, with non-food expenditure now accounting for 60% of urban consumption
- Health and wellness trends supporting demand for air fryers, steamers and alternative cooking formats, and for non-stick and specialised cookware
- Own retail contributing 7.5% of revenue, with exclusive brand outlets improving product visibility and providing direct consumer insight
- Working-capital discipline: cycle reduced from 64 days to 23 days and net debt reduced, giving greater financial flexibility for the next phase of capacity utilisation, category expansion and market development
- Headwinds acknowledged: uneven consumer demand across quarters, international trade uncertainty, commodity-price movements and foreign exchange volatility affecting the operating environment
- Indian macro backdrop cited as supportive - real GDP of 7.6% in FY 2025-26, benign inflation and an unchanged repo rate of 5.50%
- Chimney and other built-in categories supported by BIS certification and tighter safety standards raising the barrier for unorganised players
- Under the IKEA partnership the Company has been awarded three product lines, with production and revenue recognition expected to commence progressively during FY 2026-27; no order-book value is disclosed.

margins.body: Gross Margin stable at 38.6% despite commodity inflation (Aluminum/Steel) due to 10% price hikes passed in Q4; EBITDA margin expanded 113 bps to 9.5%; Opex grew 41% YoY driven by sales commissions (franchise model), freight, and warranty provisions aligned with 32% sales growth.

capital_allocation.body: Debt repayment prioritized; Shift to Franchise-Owned/Franchise-Operated (FOFO) and Company-Owned/Franchise-Operated (COFO) models to reduce capital intensity of retail expansion; Inventory stocking (45-60 days) for raw materials to hedge against metal price inflation.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Stove Kraft operates two ISO 9001:2015 certified manufacturing facilities - a larger one in Bengaluru, Karnataka and another in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh. The Bengaluru plant spans roughly 53 acres, with about one acre kept aside for future expansion, and houses supplementary backward-integration units producing glass lids, weight valves, vent tubes and gaskets; adjacent to the factory and registered office the Company operates a 1.20 lakh sq ft warehouse on 2.75 acres with storage capacity of around 25,500 pallet positions. Baddi manufactures Inner Lid Cookers. Management describes the investment of the last five years in backward-integrated manufacturing as being aimed at overcoming supply disruptions and improving gross margins, and states that the major investment cycle is now substantially complete - the capacity created provides headroom for a considerably larger business without requiring a proportionate increase in capital expenditure, making improving utilisation the driver of operating leverage, returns and cash generation over coming years. Against the IKEA supply partnership for cookware for IKEA's global store network, the Company has built a dedicated 1,80,000 sq ft manufacturing facility at Harohalli, Karnataka and invested approximately Rs 58 crore in dedicated tooling, machinery and supporting infrastructure; three product lines have been awarded, the business is expected to commence shortly, and production and revenue recognition are expected to commence progressively during FY 2026-27, with meaningful revenue contribution seen in the coming years. A Cast Iron Foundry at the Harohalli factory runs an automated line with current installed capacity of 2.2 million pieces per annum, designed to reach 4.4 million pieces per annum in future. The Company began manufacturing and selling kitchen chimneys from its own plant in Q1 FY26 and is building a full in-house manufacturing setup for all kinds of chimney, expected to take around a year, in a category placed under a Quality Control Order making BIS mandatory from 2026. Manufacturing capability is also being strengthened across Bengaluru and Baddi to support induction-cooktop demand, and production of backward-integrated kettles and cast-iron cookware was increased during FY 2025-26. On the retail side, 67 new stores were opened in FY 2025-26 taking the network to 329 outlets across 151 cities and 22 states (147 of them franchisee-operated), with a plan to add around 100 stores nationwide every year, increasingly through franchisee-operated formats focused on North and West India. On energy infrastructure, the upcoming commissioning of a 1.7 MW solar plant is expected shortly, and the Company has commissioned an RO plant and a 500 KL STP as part of a closed-loop water system.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and aggressive on volume growth (>15% guidance); Pragmatic on margins (protecting 11% EBITDA while absorbing forex hits); Transparent on accounting distortions (lease liability, supplier credit); Focused on market share leadership in induction.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Comprehensive range across price points and categories - cookware, pressure cookers, small appliances and built-ins - serving mass, semi-premium and premium consumers through a single platform
- Multi-brand architecture: Pigeon (flagship, value/award-winning), Gilma (urban design-conscious, franchisee-run exclusive outlets) and BLACK+DECKER (premium, under an exclusive brand licensing agreement with Stanley Black & Decker since 2016)
- Highly backward-integrated manufacturing - facilities produce bakelite handles, sheet metal parts, moulded components, die-cast parts, moulds, dies and fixtures, plus glass lids, weight valves, vent tubes and gaskets - reducing dependence on outside suppliers and OEMs, improving gross margins and cushioning supply disruptions
- Multi-channel distribution spanning general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce and 329 exclusive brand stores across 22 states and 151 cities, backed by 8 C&F agents, over 600 distributors and 12 separate export distributors
- In-house after-sales service with the Company's own technicians, a centralised CRM, a central call centre routing requests to branches, BIZOM for real-time field-force tracking and a Distributor Management System monitoring secondary/tertiary sales and distributor inventory
- Dedicated in-house R&D facility working alongside foreign technology partners, supported by a sourcing and quality assurance team based in China
- Early-mover position in in-house chimney manufacturing, where the QCO/BIS mandate from 2026 restricts sellers and most of the handful of domestic players rely on SKD assembly rather than full in-house production
- Historical distribution advantage from Pigeon's tie-ups with LPG distributors Indian Oil and Hindustan Petroleum, which provided a ready-made sales network for nearly a decade

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Forex volatility (significant loss in Q4); Raw material price inflation (Aluminum, Steel, Glass); Supply chain dependency on Chinese components (crystalline glass, magnets); Competition in e-commerce channel; Execution risk on rapid retail franchise rollout.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Retail store average sales increased from INR 3.8L to INR 4.7L, with breakeven at INR 2.5L, making new stores immediately accretive; Right-of-Use assets dropped from INR 160 Cr to INR 62 Cr due to accounting change (useful life reduced from 9 to 3 years), artificially depressing assets/liabilities; 97.7% volume growth in small appliances vs 12.7% value growth indicates a strategic mix shift to high-volume, lower-ASP entry-level products to capture market share.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [IKEA partnership] The milestones slide records the company having "entered into a strategic partnership with IKEA to develop cookware products" (the extract's year labels are unbound, so the date is not asserted here).
- [Demand shock] The induction upcycle is explicitly tied to an external event: "With the sudden dearth of LPG gas cylinders, the country saw a sudden spike in the purchase of induction cooktops", and the ICT commentary references "pre-war levels" — a demand driver outside management's control.
- [Working capital contradiction] The deck gives two different readings of the same 45-day figure: highlight 05 says "net working capital increased to 45 days from 23 days in Q4FY26, reflecting a strategic inventory build-up ahead of the festive season", while the working-capital note says "despite festive season inventory build-up, inventory days improved to 45 from 69 in Q1FY26". Separately the working-capital bar chart shows inventory days of 158, receivable days 28 and payable days 140 for Q1FY27 (FY25: 144/33/113; FY26: 133/26/136). Both readings are recorded as printed; no reconciliation is attempted.
- [Marketing scale] The "Ex Ko Karo Exchange" campaign reviving the Pigeon exchange offer reported 43.5 million reach, 6.3 million YouTube views, 1.27 million clicks and 30k+ high-intent leads, supported by national print ads, PR in national and vernacular publications, influencer/vox-pop content and point-of-sale branding.
- [Board addition] Mr. Chandru Kalro, former Managing Director of TTK Prestige Limited, sits on the board as Non-Executive Independent Director, bringing "over 35 years of leadership experience in the consumer durables industry" — a direct competitor pedigree on the board.
